note: See grant_contract.mjs. Entries may only be REMOVED, never edited to hide a regression. All 47 entries were found on this file's first run, by asking the database rather than reading the grant table. None had ever failed a test, because every test in this repository connects as the owner — who bypasses RLS and holds every privilege.

entries.why: hp_app and hp_reader are the only roles in this cluster that can log in, and neither holds USAGE on obs or safety. Every table grant they hold outside `public` is therefore unexercisable: the statement fails with "permission denied for schema" before the table grant is ever consulted. Verified by execution, not by reading the grant table.

entries.why: RLS is enabled on principal.patient_attribute_confirmation with no INSERT policy for confirmation_ui_role, so the confirmation UI cannot record a confirmation. Pre-existing; predates this week's work.
entries.item: R13-rls — add the missing policies. Follows R13-conn, because which roles need policies depends on which roles the app assumes.

entries.why: Migration 012 enabled RLS on this table and added no policy for redflag_role. Confirmed by execution: an INSERT of a real EMERGENCY event is refused with "new row violates row-level security policy". safety.red_flag_log got its two policies in migration 027 §5; these tables never got theirs.
entries.item: R13-rls — add the missing policies. Follows R13-conn, because which roles need policies depends on which roles the app assumes.

entries.why: Migration 030 §8 granted metrics_role SELECT on the tables the §6.5 metrics read, but those tables carry RLS with no policy for it. The metrics job would read zero rows in production and report NO_DATA for everything — a metrics module that reports nothing wrong because it can see nothing at all. My omission, found the day after J3-4 merged.

entries.why: NOLOGIN with no members, so nothing can ever assume this role. Its grants describe an intended security model rather than an operating one. This is the other half of rule A: the roles that CAN reach these schemas cannot be logged in as, and the roles that can log in cannot reach the schemas.
